slot.brief: Ask which indicator/apparatus is correct for a strong acid–strong base titration and why the burette is rinsed with the titrant first.

stem: Aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ is used to titrate $\text{HCl}$. Which choice gives a suitable indicator and correct burette-rinsing practice?
options: Use phenolphthalein in the flask; rinse the burette with $\text{NaOH}$ to prevent dilution by residual water.
Use starch in the flask; rinse the burette with $\text{NaOH}$ to prevent dilution by residual water.
Use phenolphthalein in the flask; rinse the burette with $\text{HCl}$ to prevent dilution by residual water.
Use litmus in the flask; rinse the burette with distilled water to prevent dilution by residual water.

verdicts.working: Phenolphthalein is suitable for an HCl–NaOH titration. Rinse the burette with the solution it will contain, NaOH, to avoid dilution by residual water.

working:
Phenolphthalein gives a clear endpoint in a strong acid–strong base titration.
Residual water in the burette would dilute its contents.
Rinsing with the titrant, $\text{NaOH}$, avoids changing its concentration.
